title: Dynamical correlation functions of extensive charges after global quantum quenches
authors: Riccardo Travaglino, Katja Klobas, Bruno Bertini, Pasquale Calabrese
abstract: We investigate the $n$-time cumulant generating function (or $n$-Full Counting Statistics, $n$-FCS) of extensive $U(1)$ charges following a quantum quench. Exploiting space-time duality we characterise this function when evolving from initial states that are symmetric under the action of the charge. In particular, we show that if the correlations in time are sufficiently weak, e.g.\ the transport is ballistic, the $n$-FCS factorises into a sum of single-time FCS arranged in a time-shell structure. A direct implication of this structure is a drastic simplification of dynamical correlation functions: in the presence of time ordering they only depend on the smallest time entering the correlator. We support these findings with several analytical and numerical tests performed in free and interacting models.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to calculate how extensive charges fluctuate after a quantum quench. By exploiting space-time duality and assuming weak time correlations, the authors show that complex multi-time correlation functions simplify dramatically, depending only on the earliest measurement time. This provides significant analytical simplification for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in many-body systems.
main_problem: The research focuses on characterizing the dynamical correlation functions of extensive U(1) charges following a global quantum quench.
main_result: Under conditions like ballistic transport, connected correlation functions simplify drastically, depending only on the smallest time entering the correlator. The $n$-FCS factorizes into a structure related to single-time FCS.
method: The authors employ space-time duality and analyze multi-time Full Counting Statistics (n-FCS) using techniques applicable to free fermionic systems, generalizing results to interacting models.
model_or_system: The study uses lattice Hamiltonians with a global U(1) conserved charge $Q$, often modeled via the XX chain or general free/interacting fermionic systems undergoing a quantum quench from an initial symmetric state.
key_observables: Multi-time Full Counting Statistics (n-FCS), connected time-ordered correlation functions $\langle T Q_A(t_n) \cdots Q_A(t_1) angle_c$, and the restricted charge $Q_A$ on a subsystem $A$.
important_parameters: Ballistic transport regime, large subsystem size ($\ell_A$), and the specific time ordering of measurements $\{t_i\}$.
main_assumptions: The key results are derived assuming weak time correlations (e.g., ballistic transport) and utilizing space-time duality to relate non-equilibrium dynamics to simpler structures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical tests confirming that the connected two-point function depends only on the earliest time $t_{\min}$, and show the structure of the four-point function being independent of later times.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first analyzing the n-FCS, exploiting space-time duality to derive factorization properties, and then applying these results to simplify the connected correlation functions for various time orderings.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful analytical tools (like the time-shell structure) to simplify complex non-equilibrium dynamics in many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and quantum quenches relevant to AMO physics.
